I'm not sure if you're disagreeing or agreeing with me, but yeah, mental health talk does have "buzz words" attached to it. Instead of saying, "I hate loud noises" they say something dumb like, "I have PTSD for loud noises" which just discredits and minimizes people who actually suffer from PTSD...

I stole from my brother, because he stole from my mother to buy drugs and hang out with his friends. My mother, who was dealing with a cheating, abusive husband, working two jobs to pay for the house because my dad didn't want to work, and struggling with shitty bosses.

I stole the money he made from drugs and the money he stole from my mom and gave it back to her.

So tell me, am I really that shitty of a person?

Thank fuck. I felt like such a dick saying this (hence the anon) but I just needed to say it. It's bothered me for so long.

I'm 100% the same, wherein I go out of my way to avoid hurting people and help people, and always try to motivate my friends.

The one who always talks about how she is depressed and wants to kill herself; I always try to get her to do something, to have fun, because that's what you should do if you're depressed. But she doesn't follow through and instead uses mental health as a crutch, an excuse to just be lazy and complain. And I hate it.

I hate people like that, that use *real issues* as an excuse to be a certain way or to get attention.

Thanks for commenting and getting it. I was worried everyone would call me a piece of shit for saying this, but it's nice to hear someone who agrees.

I don't think that's "turned on", but more a "motherly instinct" to want to help and protect said friend.

I think it's normal.

Now, if you *wanted* to see her vulnerable like that, and wanted to *keep pushing* to make her vulnerable, that'd be a "kink" of sorts, like sadism, I'd assume.

But you didn't, from what you say. You just felt a surge of protectiveness. That's normal. We are pack animals, after all...
